review:
Brawlhalla is that weird mix of “this is kinda fun” and “why am I still playing this.” I’ve dumped more than 700 hours into it to know the combat can be satisfying when you land a slick combo or spike someone into the void. But there’s no denying the BIG downsides.

A lot of the characters feel like copy-pastes with different skins. Not the variety the game tries to sell you. And while it’s free-to-play, some of the more appealing stuff definitely feels locked behind a “spend money or stay basic” wall. Say what you want, but the Paytolookgood energy is strong here.

And don’t even get me started on the lag. One second you’re mid-string, the next you’re teleporting into the blast zone like you just got snapped out of reality. It’s just not stable enough sometimes.

Still, it has that “one more match” pull! you’ll quit in rage, cool off, and somehow… launch it again. Not perfect, not even close, but it scratches a certain itch.

review:
Играл в эту игру несколько дней подряд, и могу сказать — впечатления крайне положительные. Атмосфера захватывает с первых минут: отличная музыка, красивая графика и продуманная детализация мира. Управление интуитивное, но при этом требует внимания и реакции, особенно в напряжённых моментах. Сюжет подаётся интересно, с элементами неожиданности, и действительно заставляет переживать за персонажей.
Отдельно хочется отметить оптимизацию — игра работает стабильно, без вылетов и лагов, что редкость в наши дни. Есть мелкие недочёты, например, не всегда удобная камера и редкие баги с физикой, но они не портят общего впечатления.
В целом — отличное сочетание геймплея, атмосферы и качества. Если вам нравятся проекты с душой и глубиной, обязательно попробуйте. Разработчикам — огромное спасибо за проделанную работу!

review:
Brawlhalla is one of those games that’s easy to pick up but surprisingly hard to master. After putting in over 37 hours, I can say it offers a solid mix of fun, chaos, and competitive challenge.

Pros:

Fast-paced gameplay: Matches are short, thrilling, and always different.

Diverse legends: Each character feels unique with their weapon combinations.

Cross-platform play: Seamless experience with friends across all devices.

Frequent updates: Ubisoft keeps the game fresh with events and new content.

Cons:

Learning curve: Getting good takes time, especially against experienced players.

Matchmaking: Can feel uneven at times, especially for mid-level players.

Visual clutter: In 4-player matches, it’s easy to lose track of your character.

Verdict:
A free-to-play brawler that’s genuinely rewarding once you get into its rhythm. Whether you’re here to casually brawl with friends or grind your way up the ranks, Brawlhalla has something for everyone.

Rating: 8.5/10 — A fun, addictive, and skill-driven fighter that keeps pulling you back for “just one more match.”

review:
🕹️ Gameplay
The gameplay is super easy to pick up and enjoyable. You get into this competitive vibe, but it’s chill — no stress, just fun matches.

🎨 Graphics & Design
The visuals are adorable and full of little details that make everything charming.

🔊 Sound & Music
We didn’t focus too much on the audio, but it blends in nicely.

👯 Fun Factor
The fun is massive! Playing with my sister and random players always turns into laughs and good times. 

💸 Pay-to-Win?
Brawlhalla is free-to-play, and yes, you can spend money to unlock characters or extras faster. But it hasn’t really bothered us so far — probably because my sister and I mostly play together, and we’re on the same level of not buying extras.

💭 Overall Impression
Brawlhalla is perfect for short sessions or casual hangouts — entertaining, lighthearted, and fun.

review:
Brawlhalla is the ultimate platforming fighting game. It is a lot like smash bros but it is more streamlined, balanced, and competitive.  The game is free and the developers respect your time and wallet.

The ELO system is fine tuned so in ranked matches you are always fighting at your own skill level and Free-For-All is a great place to learn the game and be able to kill players way better than yourself during the chaos. There is Ranked 2v2 with friendly fire enabled, making you think twice about spamming large hitboxes and it is one of my favorite things to do.  You can also create private rooms for just your friends and enjoy all of the custom game modes and maps that have been put into the game over the years including the WWE Smackdown.  

As I play this game more it becomes more fun, the trick is to not get upset when you lose and to try to learn from each defeat and improve until you can reach Valhalla.  There is a regular stream of new content and battle passes and I never feel bad paying the devs for skins and battle passes as they always deliver unique and interesting content.

As a smash vet I must say that this game has almost replaced smash bros completely for me due to the amazing balance all across the board.  Now if we can just get a Goku crossover this game would be absolutely perfect ;)

review:
I love this game and it is not *truly* about fighting. This game is about a journey. When you start playing Brawlhalla and begin to gather knowledge about the movement and what each weapon and character does, you will quickly see that the strong attacks (called signature attacks or 'sigs') are very strong... and big, thus you will encounter many players that abuse the sigs and maybe you will become one of them. As you keep playing the game, you will notice that they being big and strong have very notable trade-offs, usually being that they cabn be reacted to, so you will look for them, escape the attack and punish. When you make that realization is truly when the journey begins. You ask me "why?", well this is when the game becomes about human psychology and analysis, it is when you start adapting to other players playstyles and play accordingly, it is when the game starts teaching you about PATIENCE. And THAT is a life lesson you can take from the game.



OOOOORRRRRR, you can get sick-nasty in the complex mechanics, strings and combos this game gives you the opportunity to use and clip everybody, running over them like a truck XD. Either way, the game is very fun if you give it a try :)

review:
I am a 50 y.o. father, probably one of the oldest people playing Brawlhalla.
I am a single father to my son, who is now 14. My son recently started playing this game.
In less than a week, he had already played for over 20 hours.
This was terrible for me because it was already hard enough for me to spend time with my son
because he was always out with his friends or watching YouTube. So I decided to make a Steam
account to play with my son. I started playing, but this was my first time playing a video game
since the 90's, so I was quite lost. I asked my son for help, and together we spent some hours playing Brawlhalla with other people who were surprisingly kind.
I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my son since my wife cheated on me and died suddenly shortly after. Playing video games reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought
me and my son closer again, and now we actually spend time together outside the house as well.

review:
I believe Brawlhalla is an excellent game. At its core, it is a 2D fighting game with simple graphics. Thanks to its visual style, it doesn’t require powerful hardware to run— even the weakest of computers can handle it.

The game offers a wide variety of combo possibilities, and it features a large roster of characters. The developers actively maintain the game by continuously releasing new fighters, each with their own unique style. While it is most enjoyable when played with friends, it can also be great fun with random players or even against AI opponents.

All in all, Brawlhalla is a very accessible game that remains enjoyable without spending a single cent.

review:
Gameplay-wise, it’s a 2D PvP Platform Fighting style of game similar to the Smash Ultimate series with tons of characters. There’s 100+ characters right now and there’s still more coming out. 
The gameplay is fun and replay-able and got me through most of COVID. It’s also really fun if you have friends to play with.

The only downsides in my experience of playing this game are:
- Players are toxic. This is the case whether they’re mechanically worse than you and spam Sigs (signature special moves) and win, whether it’s a close game where the two of you were actually evenly matched, or whether they’re better than you and you get stomped. Players are toxic and this adds to the frustration of losing in this game, though the player-base being full of shitters is no fault of the game. 
- There is no chat in public lobbies. There used to be one but it got removed because players wouldn’t stop using it for trash-talking. Only custom lobbies have a chat, but why use that when you’re probably already friends and on a Discord call together? 

TLDR: the gameplay is fun, especially if you have 1-7 friends to play with. Otherwise, prepare to hate this game and its player-base with every public game you play.

review: This game is unbelievably amazing if your sole purpose in life is to have a sweaty, fat 12-year-old plow their scythe up your anal cavity and rip out all vital organs. Brawhalla's vast range of unique combos and weapons exhibits such robust creativity to the extent that players only require two brain cells to be godly in this game! Furthermore, Brawhalla’s community is truly the pinnacle of gaming culture, where many players demonstrate good sportsmanship through a variety of fun emojis! And occasionally, players wish to further connect by inviting you to custom lobbies, to enact thoughtful exchanges with one another! I am starting to lose count of the amount of times I have been told to kill myself!! This game’s only made me break two monitors! Only two!! If that’s not considered a steal, then I don’t know what is! Another positive aspect I feel is overlooked is its mysterious attributes. I will never know the degree of skill my opponent is going to have despite the claimed “accuracy” of ELO rating! Hell, I was at 1765 and plummeted back to gold! And I still got paired with Diamond Ranks! This obscure inconsistency adds a whole new excitement as I do not know what the fuck I am going to do to myself after a match! I am very appreciative of the experience Brawhalla has provided me, as it has excavated whole new emotions that I had yet to discover. To summarize, if you’re looking for that extra push to jump off that cliff or bridge, then this is the game for you!

review:
TL;DR fun if you are highly, HIGHLY competitive and willing to grind hours without much care for aesthetics. Otherwise, you can find more fun elsewhere.

This game is not for the faint of heart. To put my opinion bluntly, it feels and plays like a highly competitive hellhole. Fun is derived not from playing it as a casual player, but playing it as a hardened gladiator. This games play like Super Smash Bros minus the lively animations that make the game appear friendly, and heavy emphasis on critical, sometimes pinpoint execution. (No joke, some combos only give you 1/2 frames to follow up and are very easy to mess up.)

Of course, that is not to say that it has no casual modes. It has plenty. You can hop into a custom game with a friend and play other modes like horde, bubble tag, temple climb, kung foot, dodge bomb, snow brawl - modes that do not put a heavy emphasis on competitive and moreso on goofiness. There are even custom lobbies out there for this exact purpose. However, there are definitely better games for a more casual experience than this one.

I strongly recommend it as it does fill its niche incredibly well: a high precision fighting platformer. I only got good after sinking an ungodly amount of time in this game, and even then I am far from the top. Understandably, this is not for everyone, and entering with the wrong mindset can cause more frustration than fun. Consider yourself warned.

P.S. To put into perspective, I never won a single 1 v 1 on my first day of playing this game. However... I have been winning quite consistently since.

review:
🛡️ BRAWLHALLA: The Game Where Jumping Off the Map Is a Valid Strategy 🛡️
I downloaded Brawlhalla thinking, “Cool, Smash Bros but free.” What I got was a pixelated coliseum of chaos where Thor can fistfight SpongeBob’s cousin and lose to a sentient toaster with better spacing.
Gameplay?
It’s a platform fighter. You jump, dodge, and yeet your enemies off the stage like it’s a cosmic sumo match. Combos are crisp, movement is buttery, and every match feels like a caffeine-fueled ballet of violence. You’ll spend 30 minutes in training mode learning a 5-hit string, then get bodied by someone spamming side-sig with a smile.
Characters?
• 	Over 50 legends, each with two weapons and a dream.
• 	You’ve got sword-wielding knights, alien wrestlers, anime archers, and a literal cowgirl with a cannon.
• 	Also, crossover madness: Shovel Knight, Adventure Time, Walking Dead, and WWE. Yes, you can suplex someone off a cliff as John Cena.
Weapons?
• 	Blasters? Pew pew.
• 	Scythe? Emotional damage.
• 	Hammer? The embodiment of “I don’t know what I’m doing but it’s working.”
• 	Gauntlets? Punch first, ask questions never.
Ranked Mode?
It’s a spiritual journey. You start in Bronze, full of hope. You reach Gold, full of rage. You hit Diamond, full of existential dread. Every match is a test of patience, reflexes, and whether you can resist typing “gg ez” ironically.
Community?
• 	Half wholesome, half gremlin.
• 	You’ll get complimented for a sick combo, then emoted on for missing a recovery.
• 	The salt mines are deep, but the memes are deeper.
Final Verdict: Brawlhalla is the only game where I’ve rage quit, reinstalled, and queued again in under 60 seconds. It’s fast, fun, and free—with just enough jank to keep it spicy. Whether you’re a sweaty ranked warrior or a casual chaos gremlin, there’s a legend waiting to be your main.
10/10 would get edge-guarded by a 12-year-old again.

review:
🌟 A Free-to-Play Platform Fighter That Shines with Friends and Customization! 🌟

"Brawlhalla" is a free-to-play 2D platform fighting game that has consistently evolved since its 2017 release, offering chaotic fun for up to 8 players locally or online. With full cross-play support across PC, consoles, and mobile, it boasts a massive player base and frequent updates that keep the experience fresh . The game combines accessible controls with deep mechanics, making it easy to pick up but challenging to master.

The core gameplay involves knocking opponents off the stage using a variety of weapons and signature moves, reminiscent of titles like Super Smash Bros. Each of the 66 "Legends" has unique stats, two weapon types, and customizable cosmetics . Modes range from casual free-for-alls and ranked matches to quirky alternatives like Brawlball and Bombsketball . The recent addition of "Ascended Legends" (like Ascended Nix) introduces mythic-tier skins with enhanced visual and audio effects, adding depth to customization .

However, the game has its flaws. Public lobbies can be toxic, especially in ranked modes, and the grind for unlocking Legends or cosmetics might feel slow without purchasing the All Legends Pack ($39.99) . The reliance on RNG for some rewards and the aggressive monetization of Mammoth Coins for premium items may frustrate free players . Additionally, the simplicity of tasks in events like Brawlhalla Fest 2025 can become repetitive over time .

Pros:

🎮 Cross-Platform Play: Seamless multiplayer across PC, console, and mobile .

🎨 Deep Customization: Tons of skins, emotes, and events (e.g., Brawlhalla Fest 2025 with free rewards) .

⚔️ Varied Gameplay: Multiple modes and frequent updates keep things exciting .

🆓 Free to Play: No pay-to-win elements; all characters can be earned through gameplay .

Cons:

🗣️ Toxicity in Public Lobbies: Ranked modes often attract toxic behavior .

💰 Grindy Progression: Unlocking all Legends without paying takes time .

🔁 Repetitive Events: Some missions feel monotonous after a while .

🎲 RNG-Based Rewards: Chests and drops rely heavily on luck .


"Brawlhalla" is a standout platform fighter that excels in social play and customization. While it has issues with toxicity and monetization, its frequent updates, cross-platform support, and sheer content make it a must-try for fans of the genre. Best enjoyed with friends or in custom lobbies!

review:
I’ve been playing Brawlhalla since I was a kid, and it’s hard to put into words how much this game has meant to me. It wasn’t just a fighting game.. it was a part of my life. I played it with my best friends, cousins, my brother, and even with girls I was dating lol. It became a ritual, a bonding activity, and a source of laughter, competition, and countless memories.

What I love most about Brawlhalla is its simplicity. You can pick it up in a few minutes, but mastering it takes years. The mechanics are easy to understand, yet every character feels unique, and the endless combinations of weapons and playstyles kept me hooked. No two matches ever felt the same.

But beyond the gameplay, it was the moments that made it unforgettable.. screaming when someone pulled off a crazy recovery, laughing when a perfectly timed weapon throw ruined everything, or arguing over who really was the “best” among us. It didn’t matter if I was playing on the couch with family or online with friends across the world, Brawlhalla always brought us together.

Looking back, I realize that this game wasn’t just entertainment.. it was a backdrop for relationships, memories, and years of my life. For that, Brawlhalla will always have a special place in my heart.

Final Verdict: 10/10 - Not just a game, but a piece of my story.

review:
After spending over 1,000 hours in Brawlhalla, I can confidently say this game is the definition of “easy to learn, hard to master.”

Every legend feels like a new way to express yourself, but the real addiction is the endless mind games — predicting dodges, punishing bad habits, and pulling off a crazy edge-guard that makes you feel like a genius.

The community? Chaotic, salty, hilarious, but somehow that’s part of the charm. Ranked will humble you, customs will make you laugh, and 2v2s will ruin friendships in the best way possible.

Is it perfect? No. The balance changes sometimes feel like the devs are trolling us, and you’ll definitely meet a few spammers who seem to have one button on their keyboard. But that’s Brawlhalla: it’s messy, it’s competitive, and it’s ridiculously fun.

Would I recommend it after 1,000 hours? Absolutely. Just prepare yourself for the most intense platform fighter experience you can get for free.

10/10 would lose elo again.

review:
Дешёвая пародия
Жила была super smash bros и не тужила.. И резко появились инди энтузиасты которые на коленке склепали простую по задумке и механику игру. Анимации в игре очень дешманские, но не смотря на это смогла привлечь людей огромным количеством доната и рейтингом, конечно же (ну и привлекла электроник артс, но я уже не знаю как так получилось поэтому сказать про это не могу). Естественно на донат можно закрыть глаза, ибо игра бесплатная а скины ничего не дадут, не изменят. Но то во что сейчас (в 2024 году) превращается игра это не совсем хорошо. Персонажей добавляют и делают их всё более простыми (характеристики отличные, атаки до ужаса быстрые и идеально подходят для спама), таким образом чем легче персонаж тем лучше будет играться новичкам. Игры вымирает, но очень медленно.. Впрочем как и все игры в какой то период. Конечно как бесплатная альтернатива это великолепно, с другом поиграть прикольно. Но на постоянную игру вечером я бы посоветовал купить файтинг поинтересней. Что бы не казаться голословным скажу что у меня 1000 часов и я на самом деле не особо жалею. А также забыл добавить что есть режим тренировки, там можно опробовать любого персонажа/скин/кроссовер - это круто =)

Доступность
Большой онлайн
Уникальные механики. Много режимов и в целом функций
Огромные деньги в киберспорте. И разных матчей очень много даже сейчас (в 2024г.)
Совместимость игры, оптимизация. Тут и добавить нечего, тянуло на старом ноуте. И весит меньше гигабайта (можно быстро скачать поиграть и удалить)
Как бы странно не звучало это одна из самых сбалансированных игр, может просто файтингов. Игру всё ещё обновляют, и оружия остаются умеренными против любого другого. Единственное реально отличие персонажей это их характеристики, всё.
Дешёвая анимация, рисовка
Бравлхалла заставляет играть больше тем что бы купить лишь одного персонажа.. иногда это бывает долго и скучно, в основном для новичков
Если в игре есть баланс персонажей, то баланс поиска игр почти полностью отсутствует. В рейтинге попадаются те к кому ты ещё не готов, причём почти всегда. Единственное место где играют в основном новичковости это обычные матчи 2v2 или 1v1 (где выбирается 3 легенды). Но обычные матчи я не буду осуждать потому что это глупо тк там могут быть и сандстормы и новичковости.. если хотите по настоящему чему то научится смотрите повторы своих игр в экспериментальных матчах (режим такой)
Токсичность.. Наверное главный минус и причина выхода большинства знатоков. Возможно раньше комьюнити было чуточку лучше, но я не уверен.. Как любая игра с рейтингом тут есть ужасные и злые люди, но тут их по какой то причине намного больше, что странно для детской игры. Если новички относятся к поражению с добротой то люди кто играет уже много в 50% случаев реальные токсики.. к сожалению.

review:
Brawlhalla, despite being one of the most popular free-to-play platform fighters, has earned a reputation among many players for being frustrating to play. The core issue doesn’t lie in the graphics, mechanics, or roster of characters, but in the way the game’s design encourages certain playstyles. One of the biggest complaints is that players often spend most of the match running, jumping, and avoiding fights, only engaging in combat when it benefits them. This creates a gameplay environment that feels unfair, uncompetitive, and, ultimately, unenjoyable.

First, the movement system in Brawlhalla is extremely flexible. Players can chain dodges, jumps, and recoveries to stay airborne or keep distance almost indefinitely. While this mobility is impressive from a technical standpoint, it has the side effect of enabling extremely passive play. Instead of clashing head-on and testing skill, many players abuse the movement system to waste time and avoid taking risks.

Second, the scoring and damage systems reward this style of play. In most matches, it is advantageous to avoid fights until an opponent is already weakened, then swoop in to finish them off. This creates a “vulture” effect where players only fight when they know they can secure a knockout. As a result, genuine combat exchanges are rare, and matches often devolve into long periods of dodging followed by quick, opportunistic attacks.

Third, this behavior erodes the competitive spirit of the game. Fighting games are supposed to reward precision, timing, and skill in direct combat. But in Brawlhalla, those who want to fight aggressively are often punished by losing stocks faster, while the players who avoid conflict and play passively end up gaining the advantage. This flips the usual competitive dynamic on its head, making the game feel less about fighting and more about who can be the most annoying at avoiding conflict.

In conclusion, Brawlhalla has strong fundamentals as a fighting game, but its mechanics encourage a frustrating meta where players run, jump, and only engage when it benefits them. This passive playstyle makes the game feel “dogshit” to many players, because it robs matches of their intensity and fun. Until the developers address these design issues, the game will continue to suffer from a reputation of being more about running away than actually fighting.

review:
Brawlhalla is hands down one of my favorite games. It blends fast-paced combat with beautifully stylized graphics and smooth animations that make every match feel alive. The character designs are diverse and charming, and the stages are vibrant without being distracting.

What truly sets Brawlhalla apart is its combo system—tight, responsive, and rewarding for players who take the time to master it. Every weapon feels unique, and learning how to counter different playstyles adds depth to the experience. But beware: if you’re not skilled enough, escaping from pro players is nearly impossible. The skill ceiling is high, and that’s exactly what makes it so addictive.

review: This game is unbelievably amazing if your sole purpose in life is to have a sweaty, fat 12-year-old plow their scythe up your anal cavity and rip out all vital organs. Brawhalla's vast range of unique combos and weapons exhibits such robust creativity to the extent that players only require two brain cells to be godly in this game! Furthermore, Brawhalla’s community is truly the pinnacle of gaming culture, where many players demonstrate good sportsmanship through a variety of fun emojis! And occasionally, players wish to further connect by inviting you to custom lobbies, to enact thoughtful exchanges with one another! I am starting to lose count of the amount of times I have been told to kill myself!! This game’s only made me break two monitors! Only two!! If that’s not considered a steal, then I don’t know what is! Another positive aspect I feel is overlooked is its mysterious attributes. I will never know the degree of skill my opponent is going to have despite the claimed “accuracy” of ELO rating! Hell, I was at 1965 and plummeted back to gold! And I still got paired with Diamond Ranks! This obscure inconsistency adds a whole new excitement as I do not know what the ♥♥♥♥ I am going to do to myself after a match! I am very appreciative of the experience Brawhalla has provided me, as it has excavated whole new emotions that I had yet to discover. To summarize, if you’re looking for that extra push to jump off that cliff or bridge, then this is the game for you!

review:
At first, Brawlhalla feels like the best party you’ve ever been invited to. Bright colors, chaotic maps, and characters flying across the screen like fireworks—it’s pure joy in motion. You throw out random attacks, accidentally land a combo, and suddenly you feel like a professional esports player. It’s lighthearted, fun, and endlessly replayable.

Then… something changes.

Your opponents stop being silly little cartoon characters and start transforming into omnipotent gods with the reflexes of lightning itself. That Orion across the stage? He’s not just another player, he’s an eldritch being who has calculated your every button press before you even touch the controller. Every weapon you pick up feels like a pool noodle while theirs is a divine hammer forged in the molten heart of a dying star.

And this is where the spiral begins.

Your cheerful “just one more match” becomes “I must ascend past mortality itself to land a single hit.” Every dodge is punished. Every jump is countered. Every stock you lose is another piece of your soul evaporating into the void. The music doesn’t sound playful anymore—it’s a funeral march. The stages don’t look colorful—they’re mocking you, every platform a reminder of your inevitable downfall.

By the tenth loss in a row, you’re no longer playing Brawlhalla. Brawlhalla is playing you. The game devours your hope, your joy, your sanity. The screen flashes “KO!” and you don’t even see it anymore—it’s just another reminder that everything is temporary, fleeting, doomed to collapse into dust.

And yet… the moment the match ends, your finger twitches. You press “Play Again.” Because deep down, you don’t want freedom. You want to burn with the game. To go down swinging in the eternal digital colosseum.

10/10. Would suffer again.

review: Brawlhalla is like a chaotic family reunion where everyone settles arguments by punching each other off floating platforms… and somehow it’s fun. It’s a free-to-play platform fighter with a colorful roster of legends, from sword-wielding knights to kung fu frogs (okay, maybe not frogs, but it feels like there should be). Matches are fast, silly, and full of “oops” moments — like when you try a heroic leap and just yeet yourself into the abyss. The controls are easy to learn, but the mind games and combos can get deep, especially when you’re trying to dodge that one guy who’s clearly been playing since the dawn of time. Whether you’re brawling online, with friends, or against bots, it’s pure, ridiculous fun.

review: You're considering this game because you like playing smash with your friends and online, right? Think again. You know that one friend who's an absolute sweat and knows that one Bayonetta combo that instantly kills you? 85% of people in casual matches are that person. Ranked is even worse. If you're lucky, you'll get some good matches on occasion. My character recommendation is the furry bird, no one plays her and her moves are pretty good, at least for a casual player. If you're going against the sweats you're cooked as most characters because you don't have a shield button like in smash. There's no shield. At all. No stopping the equivalent to Metaknight's side-B. This entire game would be fixed if they simply added that. That being said, I did humiliate a twitch streamer who was a sweat the other day, so it can be fun at times. I joined their stream and they were banging on their table :3 7.5/10 would reccomend because the game is fun overall, they should just force people who are sweats to play in ranked.

review:
In general a good game. 
Positives:
If you play it with friends, you can have the fun of your life.
It is the best fighting platfomer on pc. 
The thing that kept me hooked was that you can learn a weapon an then pick up almost every legend with it. After that you have a solid stable on learning new weapons.
The game has satisfying combo gameplay if you play combo weapons.
It has good balancing in general, so that you can play anything you want and have success with it.

Negatives:
If you hop into experimental(Unranked 1v1) you are just matched with 12 year old kids that are sweating their a** of or toxic people. Dont even get me started on enemys that are just spamming one move (not sig spamming) or playing passive af. 
There is nothing like a chill session of Brawl if you are not high elo and know everything about the game.
Monitisation was good until they added bundels and sidekicks imo.

In general i would recommend the game, because the moments you can have with your friends (and with the game in general) outweigh the neagtives

review: Brawlhalla. I have experienced more desk slamming rage in this game than almost any other. (Except overwatch that game stole 3,000 hours of my life and should condemned to hell) despite this intense anger each day I start it up and play again. This is the platform fighter for anyone who wants a highly competitive skill based game. In lower ranks you’ll want to claw your eyes out as you get spammed and absolutely dominated by certain weapons or abilities. While balancing does have a part to play these tactics can easily be outplayed by investing just a little bit of time into actually developing your skill at the base mechanics. I have sunk 700 hours and at least a 1,000 dollars into this game and I will continue to. Play with friends or descend into the burning hell of the ranked ladder and you will have fun. It’s all worth it for when you finally hit that one combo or hit every dodge read on a higher ranked player. I recommend this game if you are looking for an extremely competitive experience. Otherwise go play smash or something.

review:
I’ve sunk more hours into Brawlhalla than I’m proud to admit—and I regret none of it. Unlike most fighters out there, this game doesn’t overwhelm you with fancy mechanics or pay-to-win nonsense. It’s raw, fast-paced, and addictive in the best way. Matches are short but intense, and the satisfaction of landing a perfect dodge into a KO? Unmatched.

What keeps me coming back is the character variety and community vibe. There’s a legend for every playstyle, and mastering them feels genuinely rewarding. Whether it’s ranked rage or casual chaos, I’m always feeling something. Most games get stale after a while, but with frequent updates, seasonal events, and straight-up good design, Brawlhalla hasn’t lost its grip on me.

Compared to other platform fighters, Brawlhalla just gets me. It doesn’t try too hard—it just delivers. No flashy cinematics or unnecessary frills. Just pure gameplay, clutch moments, and hype. If you're debating downloading it, do it. But fair warning: you might not stop.

👍 Would recommend. Would rage. Would still come back for more.

review:
THE ULTIMATE REVENGE ARC

My friends invited me to play Brawlhalla.
I thought, “Oh cool, free game. Probably some fun party vibes.”

I picked a character with a sword. I don’t even remember who.
They told me to press buttons. I did.
They didn’t.

They juggled me. Threw me off the map. Taunted.
One of them said, “Skill issue.”
Another changed their name mid-game to “EZClapVaibhav" 

I was humiliated.

That night I didn’t sleep.
I watched combos on YouTube. I trained in the lab.
I studied movement tech like it was the SAT.
I downloaded finger-stretching exercises.
I mained Mordex.

Two weeks later, I invited them for a rematch.

They laughed.
They shouldn’t have.

First stock? Gone in 14 seconds.
Second stock? Zero-to-death with side light reads.
Final stock? I didn’t even move. I just threw my weapon and taunted.

I didn’t just beat them.
I emotionally destabilized them.

They haven’t logged on since.

Now strangers message me “pls 1v1.”
I say nothing. I just queue.

Brawlhalla didn’t just change me.
It awakened me.

review:
Brawlhalla stands as an enticing entry in the free-to-play fighting game arena, offering a refreshing, accessible take on the platform fighter genre. Its vibrant art style, diverse roster of "Legends" (characters), and intuitive two-button attack system make it incredibly easy to pick up and play for an hour or an evening. The game truly shines in its fast-paced, chaotic glory, especially when bouncing around with friends in casual modes. There's a genuine thrill in landing a devastating string of attacks, spiking an opponent off the stage, or pulling off a clutch recovery. For a game that costs nothing to download, Brawlhalla delivers undeniable moments of pure, unadulterated fun.

However, Brawlhalla's gleaming facade can quickly crack, revealing a core frustration that has plagued its community for years: the prevalence of arguably 'spammy' and overwhelmingly dominant weapon types, most notoriously the Lance.

The Lance, in particular, often transforms what should be a delightful brawl into a maddening exercise in futility. Its incredibly long-reaching, swift, and often juggle-heavy attacks can feel less like a skilled opponent outmaneuvering you and more like an unavoidable, relentless assault. While every weapon has its strengths and weaknesses, the Lance often feels disproportionately rewarded for what appears to be repetitive, low-effort inputs. You'll find yourself on the receiving end of what feels like an endless chain of dash attacks, aerials, and side-airs, leaving you bouncing uncontrollably across the stage with little room to retaliate or even breathe.

It's not just the Lance; other weapons like the Axe and Greatsword, when wielded by players focused solely on repeatedly executing their most effective (and often safest) combos, can induce a similar sense of helplessness. This isn't about tactical defeat where you acknowledge a superior player; it's about the soul-crushing sensation of being completely overwhelmed, experiencing what many frustrated players bluntly describe as being "gimped" or "raped" by a character's often low-effort, high-reward attack patterns. The joy of the fight evaporates, replaced by a bitter sense of exploitation as your stocks vanish, leaving you feeling less outplayed and more just... abused.

In essence, Brawlhalla is a fantastic time when its core mechanics lead to varied, strategic, and engaging combat. But that enjoyment comes with a significant asterisk. It's incredibly fun when you're duking it out with opponents who use their full kit, adapt, and create interesting exchanges. It's dramatically less so when you're on the receiving end of a relentless barrage from a Lance or other similarly aggressive, 'spammy' characters, leaving you feeling more like a punching bag than a participant in a fair fight. If you can stomach that particular flavor of frustration, there's a lot to love, but be warned: your fun is highly conditional on who you're matched against.

review:
Balanced and fun competitive game with a lot of skill expression.

As with many fighting games, it's not very beginner-friendly, and I highly recommend watching a brief video on weapon combos/strings since they are actually pretty easy to learn. Plenty of people complain about sig spamming and broken weapons, and I agree that for beginners, dealing with sigs can be very frustrating. However, I consider the game to be pretty well balanced overall. Every character and every weapon is viable, and although some may be stronger than others at certain times, the devs consistently push out balance patches to try to make it fair. There's also enough skill expression such that there's always an opportunity to outplay your opponent.

Please fix the mac client though, it's unplayable with constant frame dips.

review:
Highly Recommended
✅ (Been playing since near launch)
Posted June 2025

Brawlhalla is honestly one of my favorite beat 'em up games of all time. I started playing around the time it first launched, and even back then—when there were barely any characters—it was a blast.

Despite having fewer attack inputs compared to something like Super Smash Bros., the gameplay felt tight, fast, and incredibly balanced. What really impressed me was how no two matches ever felt the same. Even with a smaller roster early on, the mechanics were strong enough to keep things fresh and fun.

It’s the kind of game that’s easy to pick up, but with enough depth to stick around. Whether you’re playing casually or going sweaty in ranked, Brawlhalla holds up.

review:
[h1] The Game Stays the Same... [/h1]

New collaborations.
More characters.
More stages.
And the same frantic, lighthearted, fun spirit.
Here, the only thing you need is just the will to have fun, to try, to laugh when you get blasted off the map,
or when you land that miraculous hit at the last second.


[h2] The Tryhard Hell [/h2]


But let’s be real.
Brawlhalla has a dark side.
No, not the lore.
The tryhards.

Players who treat this like Olympic qualifiers.
People who don’t play: they execute.
People who don’t laugh: they calculate.

And then it becomes another game.
A more tense, more brutal one.
One where, if you’re still laughing,
it’s probably because you haven’t seen the infinite aerial combo that’s about to make you reflect on your life choices.


[h2] Conclusion [/h2]


Brawlhalla is a game to play with friends.
To laugh your ass off.
To trash-talk lovingly and go another round.
Not to suffer in ranked.

review:
Honestly, Brawlhalla is just a super fun game. I started playing it not expecting much, but I quickly got hooked. It’s easy to pick up, even if you’re not great at fighting games. The controls are simple, but the gameplay still has depth, so you can actually get better and learn cool strategies over time.

One thing I really like is how many characters (Legends) there are — each one feels different, so you’re not stuck doing the same thing over and over. Plus, the game is totally free, and you can even play with friends on different consoles, which is awesome.

I’d recommend Brawlhalla to anyone who likes fast-paced games or wants something competitive without being too serious. Whether you’re playing casually or trying to climb the ranked ladder, it’s just a great time. And the devs are always adding new stuff, so it never really gets boring.

review:
I've played Brawlhalla for around 4 hours and really enjoyed it. The controls are tight and responsive, and the combat feels smooth and fast-paced. It’s easy to get into, but there’s clearly a lot of depth to master.

However, I did notice some lag during online matches — which was surprising since I have a stable 100 Mbps connection. After checking, I realized the issue isn’t with speed, but likely due to server lag or high ping. It could also be the server region or Wi-Fi instability, even though everything else works fine online.

If the netcode or regional matchmaking gets a bit more optimized, this would be a solid 5-star game. Still, it’s an awesome free-to-play experience and definitely worth trying if you enjoy fighting games.

review:
Brawlhalla is a free-to-play platform fighter that blends chaotic brawling with a diverse roster of characters. With about 68 hours played, I wouldn’t call myself a high-level player—but I’ve had plenty of fun, especially with friends. That said, it’s definitely a game that shines in the right context.

🟢 Pros:
Super Fun with Friends
This is where Brawlhalla really comes to life. Whether it’s 1v1s, team fights, or chaotic 4-player free-for-alls, it’s easy to jump in and start having a blast. It’s the kind of game that’s best enjoyed with some friendly trash talk and laughter.

Easy to Learn, Hard to Master
The controls are accessible, and you can start pulling off cool moves pretty quickly. But once you start climbing the skill curve, you’ll realize there’s a surprising amount of depth—timing, spacing, matchups, and movement all matter a lot.

Big Roster of Unique Characters
With tons of Legends and crossover characters, there’s something for everyone. Each weapon combo feels different, which keeps things fresh.

Free-to-Play Without Being Pay-to-Win
You can unlock everything through gameplay, and purchases are mostly cosmetic. That’s a big plus.

🔴 Cons:
Not as Fun Solo
While it’s a solid game overall, playing solo just doesn’t have the same appeal. Without friends, the fun and chaos feel a bit hollow, and ranked mode can feel frustrating or overly sweaty if you're not trying to "git gud."

Learning Curve Can Get Steep
Once you hit a certain skill level (or face players who live in ranked), the gap becomes noticeable. It’s not a huge issue, but casual players might feel outpaced.

Repetitive if You're Not Progressing
If you're not working toward a rank or grinding for unlocks, the matches can start to feel samey after a while—especially solo.

Final Thoughts:
Brawlhalla is a blast when played with friends. It’s approachable, fun, and has enough depth to keep you coming back—if you have the right group to enjoy it with. On your own, it’s a bit less compelling, but still a solid, well-made fighter that deserves its spot in the genre.

Rating: 7.5/10 – A party brawler at heart. Great with friends, less so solo—but always solid.

review:
🛡️ Brawlhalla - Fun, Fast, and Free
Brawlhalla is one of those games that’s easy to pick up, but hard to master. It looks simple at first, but there’s a lot of depth once you get into it.

What I Like:

Tons of unique characters (called Legends), each with different weapons and styles.

The combat is smooth, fast-paced, and really fun.

You can play online, offline, ranked, or just casually with friends.

Cross-platform works great — I play with friends on console while I'm on PC.

It’s completely free and not pay-to-win.

What I Don’t Like:

Some matchmaking can feel unfair, especially at low ranks.

The community can be toxic sometimes, like in most competitive games.

Cosmetics are a bit expensive if you care about looks.

Still, I keep coming back because it’s just that fun. Whether you're messing around in free-for-alls or going all-in on ranked 1v1s, Brawlhalla delivers.

Final : 8.5/10 — Worth playing, especially with friends.

review:
Was curious to see how this outlasted so many other platform fighters. It's because it's so accessible. Simple attacks allow players to focus more on dashing, air juggling and edge guarding. Characters each have two unique combinations of weapons with their own flair on special attacks and some minor stat differences. Currently a 61 character roster but it's not as though you have to learn 61 matchups and you can just play whoever looks the coolest.

Free to play and cross-play make finding a game near instantaneous. Ranked 1v1 and 2v2. Taunts and post fight emojis (albeit toxic). Rage quitters turn into bots. All characters are unlockable through an easily obtainable currency. Cosmetics cost a premium but nobody is making you buy them.

review:
Please ignore the mouth breathers with 2k hours leaving negative reviews, their brains can't comprehend the idea that them spending thousands of hours on a game might mean they actually like it despite its flaws.

Its a free game that provides very solid competitive platform fighting gameplay, and is especially good with friends due to how easy it is to play together. The game balance and monetization (they just released a 35 dollar skin) can be frustrating/poor at times but, again, it is a free video game. You lose nothing trying it out. 

With that being said, this is one of those games with a very high skill ceiling and a community that has spent thousands of hours perfecting the mechanics, so being a new player can be rough. Despite what some people may say, pretty much every match is decided by who is the better player. There isn't much you can do about other than just buckling up and learning the game or bringing a friend along to make practicing more fun. 

The community can also be quite toxic at times, but that is the nature of basically any competitive video game, you'll be able to get over it. 

Lastly there is rollback netcode, which can make things feel a bit clunky or laggy at times (sometimes your game will make a sound that you hit someone but they won't actually get hit), but is ultimately more positive than negative as it makes the game less ping dependent.

review: Brawlhalla is a very exciting and dynamic fighting game that I have enjoyed playing since 2018. review:
Brawlhalla is a fun, fast-paced platform fighter that’s easy to jump into but offers a ton of depth for those who want to master it. The controls are smooth and responsive, and each Legend brings their own unique flair with different weapons and playstyles. Whether you're playing casually with friends or diving into ranked matches, there's always a good time to be had.

One of the best things about Brawlhalla is its accessibility. It's free to play, supports cross-platform multiplayer, and doesn’t overwhelm new players with complicated mechanics. The game is constantly updated with new content, events, and characters — including fun crossovers that bring in popular franchises for a fresh twist.

It’s a great choice for fans of competitive brawlers or anyone looking for a fun, skill-based game with a lighthearted vibe. Brawlhalla may look simple on the surface, but it’s packed with satisfying gameplay, strong community support, and endless replayability.

review:
I've been playing this game for 120 hours in less than two months, and honestly, these have been the most frustrating two months of my life.
It feels like there are four types of players in this game:
The Normal One – Just plays the game normally. Unfortunately, almost no one does this.
The Jumper – Feels like his mom was bouncing on a trampoline while giving birth and decided to name him Spacebar.
Spam Sig – These people wake up and think, "How can I be as annoying as possible today?" Oh, right—by spamming signatures! They're usually not even good, they just win because they don’t let you touch them. I sincerely wish you all mental peace.
Passive Player – Just runs to the other side of the stage and waits for you to attack. They also jump a lot, and honestly, I have no clue how they enjoy the game.

That being said, the game is super fun, and nothing beats playing with your friends. I've already spent around $60 on skins, and I gotta say—it was worth it. The skins really make the experience feel different.
Do not play this game unless you know someone who's good at it, because progressing alone is insanely hard.
I’d give the game a 7/10, which is honestly pretty generous. It’s a simple game, but hey, it kills time.

review:
Brawlhalla is a fast-paced, fun, and highly competitive platform fighter that I’ve been playing for a long time. With a huge roster of characters, cross-platform play, and frequent updates, it’s one of the best free-to-play fighting games available. The gameplay is easy to pick up but hard to master, making it accessible for casual players while still offering deep mechanics for those who want to compete seriously.

One of Brawlhalla’s biggest strengths is its variety, different weapons, legends, and game modes keep things fresh. The movement and combat feel smooth, and every match is a mix of skill, strategy, and fast reactions. However, the game does have balance issues at times, and some mechanics (like dodge reads and certain weapon metas) can feel frustrating.

Despite that, Brawlhalla remains a solid fighting game that doesn’t rely on pay-to-win mechanics, every legend can be unlocked through gameplay. Whether you’re playing casually with friends or grinding ranked matches, it’s a game that keeps pulling you back in. If you enjoy platform fighters, this is one you should definitely try

review:
Ah, Brawlhalla—a veritable ballet of digital destruction, a symphony of steel and sorcery, a grand coliseum where pixelated warriors clash in an eternal tempest of skill and chaos! To call this mere “game” would be an insult of the highest order; nay, it is a testament to the boundless ingenuity of humankind’s foray into the realm of electronic gladiatorial combat.

Gameplay – A Dance of the Divine (10/10)
The very act of engaging in Brawlhalla’s combat is akin to partaking in a celestial waltz—each strike, each dodge, each weapon toss a perfectly choreographed note in the opera of battle. One does not simply "fight" in Brawlhalla; one ascends beyond mortal comprehension, grasping the esoteric artistry of aerial movement and edge-guarding with a reverence reserved only for the finest of martial philosophies.

Characters – A Pantheon of Unparalleled Valor (9/10)
The warriors of Brawlhalla, known as Legends, are a collection so vast and varied that one might suspect the gods themselves curated them from the annals of myth and history. From valiant knights to intergalactic bounty hunters, each Legend wields their weapons with a finesse that would make even the most seasoned warriors weep tears of admiration. And let us not forget the crossovers—why, where else may one witness the ungodly spectacle of Finn the Human battling Ezio Auditore in an aerial duel of destiny?

Graphics – A Feast for the Retinal Orbs (8/10)
The art style is nothing short of a visual serenade—a colorful, whimsical aesthetic that masks the true brutality lurking beneath. Every map, every explosion, every perfectly timed ground-pound is rendered in an animated splendor that does not seek to overwhelm but instead beckons the eye with a playful invitation to destruction.

Soundtrack – A Symphony of Smashing (8/10)
The music, while often overlooked, provides a gallant backdrop to the carnage. It is neither intrusive nor lackluster, but rather a noble accompaniment to the havoc unfolding upon the screen. A melody to which one shall undoubtedly lose many a battle but do so with the grandeur befitting a fallen champion.

Final Verdict – A Game Worthy of the Digital Pantheon (9/10)
To play Brawlhalla is to enter an arena where only the most cunning, the most dexterous, and the most gloriously unhinged shall prevail. It is an experience both exhilarating and humbling, a reminder that in the grand stage of digital combat, one’s triumphs are fleeting, but the pursuit of mastery is eternal.

Would I recommend this exquisite title? Verily, with the force of a thousand Thor hammers. Download it, embrace the chaos, and prepare thyself for a journey of unparalleled spectacle.

Review: Brawlhalla

Brawlhalla, as a free-to-play fighting game, has managed to maintain a relatively consistent and sizable community for years. In the following review, I want to share my thoughts on why that might be the case.

Gameplay:

Unlike other games in the genre, such as Mortal Kombat, Street Fighter, or Injustice, Brawlhalla features a much simpler combat system. There are light and heavy attacks, each of which depends on the character you’re playing, the weapons they are using, and the direction in which the attack is executed.
For example, a side attack with blasters has a different range, hitbox position, and speed than an side attack with a greatsword.

This means that each legend plays completely differently. However, with light attacks, combos can be performed that, depending on the stats, can also be executed by other legends if they are using the same weapons. This creates a sweet spot in the category of "easy to learn, hard to master," making the game accessible to a large audience.

Story:

Brawlhalla doesn’t have a traditional story, but you can read through various entries to learn more about the lore of the characters.

Graphics:

The game features an art style that gives it a relatively timeless visual appeal. I find it simple yet beautifully designed.

Conclusion:

Brawlhalla is a fighting game that, by being free-to-play and easy to learn, continues to attract a large number of players even today. It convinces with a blend of simplicity and a touch of complexity.

Personally, even after several years, I still enjoy jumping into a few matches of Brawlhalla or even ranked mode from time to time. If what I’ve described sounds interesting to you, I highly recommend giving it a try.

That’s it for this review. See you in the Brawl. Until then!

Saderhorn

Smooth meaning the flow of a match is much less slow and heavy than most other fighting games i have played. The maps are simple but i prefer omega type maps anyway while the art is amazing say what you will about the game but the style such as backgrounds of the arena to the ui of the starting menu you can tell the artist for this game went/go ham. The cosmetics/monetization are a little to be desired the devs often give the same charters new skins rarely do you see the less used characters getting skins both battlepass and shop (i might just be projecting cuz i main shark but still). I like the cosmetics that come from battlepasses but does a fighting game really need one especially if you cant get the next battlepass with the coins received (its locked behind a money only paywall) and a single skin costing 6 bucks is just plain dumb for how little you actually get and that's not even mentioning that colab skins are going up in price more and more (there is more issues i have but basically most cosmetics aren't worth it). I will end it with this i thinks brawl is one of the better fighing games out there but the community is full of awful people and the monetization is getting out of hand but i think it is worth playing if you like smash bros types of fighting games but want something less clunky (ps if you arent enjoying it try getting high it helped me)

review: Brawlhalla is a platformer fighter that does take some inspiration from SSB (Super Smash Bros) but has very unique twist. One of them being unique weapons and unique stats making every character different from one another. They also have different modes like Ranked and just "Play" which is a bit more fun and casual. Yes this game is free to play which means it has a battle pass and premium currency, but you can still get legends with gold by just playing the game. Brawlhalla as has a feature where you can watch videos and every 10 views gets you different cosmetics or just more coins. The only downside to this is that it has a cool down which means you have to wait an amount of time before watching more videos, but the best thing about this is every 50 views it gets you a grand chest! This contains the one thing that everyone wants but is locked behind a paywall... legend skins! Now you can get legend skins from every 50 views but that takes time and you are not guaranteed to get skins. One mistake I had is that there are weekly legends and when you first play the game you better choose one and learn the character a little and start earning gold because if you want to fully unlock the character you need 5400 gold on average (some are lower) for the character. I had taken a liking to a character and one day it was swapped out of weekly rotation, this made me stop playing the game which I regret because it is so fun. Highly recommend! (I have not made a purchase on this game nor gotten any paid things for free)

review:
Brawlhalla is what happens when you mix Smash Bros.-style combat with a free-to-play model that actually works. With over 50 legends, cross-platform play, and fast-paced brawling, it’s one of the best F2P fighting games out there. But is it for everyone?

The Good:
✅ Tons of Characters & Crossovers: From Rayman to WWE superstars, the roster keeps growing.
✅ Easy to Learn, Hard to Master: Simple controls but deep mechanics make it great for casuals and pros alike.
✅ Frequent Updates: New legends, skins, and balance patches keep things fresh.
✅ Cross-Platform & Stable Netcode: Play with friends on any platform with smooth online matches.

The Bad:
❌ Monetization Can Be Annoying: While the game is free, unlocking legends without spending money takes time.
❌ Floaty Combat Feel: Some players might not enjoy the aerial-heavy movement style.
❌ Matchmaking Can Be Hit or Miss: Ranked can sometimes feel unbalanced, especially for new players.

Final 
Brawlhalla is one of the best free-to-play fighters around, offering fun combat and a growing community. While it may not replace Smash Bros., it holds its own as a fantastic alternative for PC and consoles.

⭐ 8/10 – FREE, fun, and surprisingly deep!

review:
Rating: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️✨ (6.5/10)

Brawlhalla is a free and accessible fighting game that offers fast and chaotic combat in the style of Super Smash Bros., but with its own approach. It is ideal for casual matches with friends or for those looking for a light alternative to the combat platform genre.

With a huge roster of characters, including crossovers with popular franchises, Brawlhalla bets on variety and visual spectacle. The mechanics are easy to learn, and that makes it a good gateway for new players. In addition, its availability on multiple platforms with crossplay is a big plus.

The competitive mode exists, but its ranking and matchmaking system leaves something to be desired compared to other more polished fighters. The experience is sometimes affected by lag or disconnections, and although it has an active base, the game fails to maintain the same level of refinement in the competitive scene.

📉 Added to that, its monetization model with rotation of characters and cosmetics can be frustrating for those looking for a more complete experience without spending money.

🎯 Conclusion:
Brawlhalla is a fun and light game, ideal for casual sessions and online parties, but it falls short in depth and balance for the most demanding of the genre. It has potential, but it is noticeable that it prioritizes accessibility over complexity.

A good pastime, but not an unforgettable fighting title.

review:
A Fun and Free Platform Fighter with Endless Action!

Brawlhalla is an exciting and highly accessible platform fighter that delivers fast-paced action, a huge roster of characters, and smooth gameplay—all for free! Whether you're a casual player looking for fun or a competitive gamer aiming to master its mechanics, there's something here for everyone.

The game features a diverse selection of Legends, each with unique weapons and playstyles. The controls are simple to learn but offer surprising depth, making skillful plays and combos very rewarding. With multiple game modes, including ranked matches, casual brawls, and custom lobbies, the variety keeps things fresh. Plus, frequent updates and crossover events (featuring characters from other franchises) add to the excitement.

However, Brawlhalla does have a few downsides. The matchmaking can sometimes feel unbalanced, especially for new players facing more experienced opponents. The free-to-play model is fair, but unlocking all Legends takes time unless you buy the All Legends Pack. Some players may also prefer a more traditional fighting game feel, as Brawlhalla's mechanics lean heavily into mobility and weapon-based combat.

Overall, Brawlhalla is a fantastic platform fighter that’s easy to pick up but hard to master. If you enjoy games like Super Smash Bros. and love fast, skill-based combat, this is definitely worth playing!

Rating: 8.5/10

review: Brawlhalla is the kind of game that sneaks up on you, promising a quick match and then trapping you in its colorful, combo-filled grip for hours on end. The charm of this 2D fighter lies in its accessibility; it's easy to pick up, hard to put down, and the cross-platform play means your friends are always a match away, no matter their device. The Legends are diverse and the action is fast, ensuring that each battle is a unique challenge. While the community can sometimes be a rough place, with toxicity rearing its ugly head, the developers are continually working to foster a more positive environment. The game's free-to-play model is refreshingly straightforward, with no pay-to-win mechanics in sight. It's a game that can be as competitive as you want it to be, with ranked modes to test your skills, or as casual as a Sunday afternoon with friends. Brawlhalla isn't just a game; it's a digital arena where friendships are forged and rivalries are born. So, grab your controller and get ready to brawl – just don't blame me if you find yourself scheduling your day around your next match.

review:
Finally a balanced 1v1 game that isn't chess, is extremely skill based and has an e-sports scene so I can learn from the pros. What else can you ask for? Transcend the team-based bot/blame mentality and play this instead. Trust me. The dopamine hits are much better when you count on yourself and win. Like, no one to blame. And it gets really intense at times too. So much fun.


Edit at 20h: Game still great.


Edit at 46h: Reached gold for the first time. Still having fun improving and chilling out. Still think this is the perfect game.

Edit at 80h: Still enjoying the game. I wouldn't say I improved all that much but I've been experimenting and decided on what I want to main and sort of have a better understanding of the game now. Still need a lot of practice though.

After 100h edit: Still good game to jump into and play. Does something that no other game does. Which is a continuous feedback loop without needing to think, only to act.

117h: Basically this is the only game that creates a unique immersion where you don't need to think, because the game doesn't give you enough time to think. So you have to constantly: act, react, feedback, adjust, repeat. That kinda loop is rare, because most games are too slow for that. They give people time to think. This is actual competition. And therefore it's one of a kind. Most games will either have levels as an advantage or positioning or give you time to think and outplay. This game doesn't do any of that. Actual perfect balance, because a hit always does the same damage. 
Okay I praised it enough now. xD

Dear Brawlhalla Team,

I wanted to share my experience with your game because, while I love playing Brawlhalla, it has been having a serious negative impact on my life. The competitive nature of the game has caused me to lose friends, as frustration and arguments have become more frequent. I find myself getting overly stressed and emotionally drained, and it's even driving me toward unhealthy habits like drinking just to cope with the frustration.

I know games are meant to be fun and challenging, but when a game starts affecting mental health this much, it’s a problem. I don’t know if it's the ranked system, the matchmaking, or just how intense the game is, but I feel like it’s pushing me toward a breaking point. I wanted to reach out in hopes that you consider how the game's structure might be impacting players' well-being. Maybe implementing better anti-tilt measures, balance adjustments, or community support features could help.

I appreciate the work you put into the game, but I needed to express how it's affecting me. Thanks for taking the time to listen.

Sincerely,

review:
Brawlhalla is a fast-paced, fun, and accessible platform fighter that’s perfect for both casual and competitive players. The game’s simple controls make it easy to pick up, but the depth in mechanics allows for plenty of room to master your favorite characters. The roster is huge, with diverse fighters, each offering unique moves and playstyles.

The graphics are bright and appealing, and the game runs smoothly across all platforms. Plus, the cross-play feature ensures you can easily find opponents, no matter what system they’re on. While the matchmaking can sometimes feel a bit unbalanced, the game’s overall gameplay and frequent updates keep things exciting and fresh.

If you’re into platform fighters, Brawlhalla offers a great free-to-play experience with lots of content to enjoy. It’s a blast to play solo or with friends!

review:
🎯 Rating: 8.0/10

📜 Overview
Brawlhalla, developed by Blue Mammoth Games, is a free-to-play 2D platform fighter that offers fast-paced, accessible combat with a focus on competitive play. Players can choose from a diverse roster of characters, each with their own unique weapons and abilities, and battle it out in various game modes. Featuring both online and local multiplayer, Brawlhalla appeals to casual and competitive players alike, offering a fun, dynamic experience that's easy to pick up but hard to master.

🌟 Pros
✅ Free-to-Play Model: Completely free to download and play with no pay-to-win mechanics.
✅ Diverse Roster: Over 40 unique characters, each with distinct movesets and playstyles.
✅ Cross-Platform Play: Seamless online play across multiple platforms, including PC, consoles, and mobile.
✅ Accessible Yet Deep: Simple mechanics for casual play, but plenty of depth for competitive players.
✅ Frequent Updates: Regular content updates, including new characters, skins, and events.

⚠️ Cons
❌ Monetization: In-game purchases for cosmetics and characters can feel grindy or expensive.
❌ Steep Learning Curve: While accessible, mastering the game’s mechanics takes time and practice.
❌ Matchmaking Issues: Some players report inconsistent matchmaking, especially in ranked modes.
❌ Lack of Single-Player Content: Limited solo options, with a focus on multiplayer modes.
❌ Repetitive Gameplay: Matches can feel repetitive, especially in the absence of more complex game modes.

💬 Player Sentiment
Positive Reviews: Players enjoy the diverse character roster, fluid combat mechanics, and the competitive scene. The cross-platform play and frequent updates keep the game feeling fresh.

Negative Reviews: Some players are frustrated by the grind for unlockables, matchmaking issues, and the limited solo play options.

🎯 Target Audience
🔹 Fans of fast-paced platform fighters.
🔹 Players who enjoy competitive online multiplayer.
🔹 Gamers looking for a free-to-play, accessible fighting game with depth.

🏆 Rating Breakdown
🎮 Gameplay: 8/10
🎨 Visuals: 7.5/10
⚖️ Balance: 8.5/10
🔄 Replayability: 8/10
👥 Community: 8/10
⭐ Overall Experience: 8.0/10

🎨 Visual Summary
🎮 Gameplay: Accessible and fast-paced with a solid mix of simplicity and depth.
🎨 Visuals: Bright, colorful character designs and environments, though basic.
⚖️ Balance: Generally well-balanced, though some characters may feel overpowered at times.
🔄 Replayability: High due to the variety of characters and game modes.
👥 Community: Active and dedicated, with regular tournaments and events.

🎯 Final Verdict
Brawlhalla is a fun, accessible platform fighter that has something for both casual players and those looking for competitive action. While its monetization model can be grindy, and some matchmaking issues may detract from the experience, the game’s diverse roster, fluid gameplay, and frequent updates make it a strong contender in the genre. Whether you're playing casually with friends or climbing the ranked ladder, Brawlhalla offers plenty of value for players looking for an exciting, free-to-play brawler.

review:
Overall, 4.49/5.00 stars.

As a long time, multi-platform, high-rank player of Brawlhalla, it is genuinely good. The game has simple to learn mechanics, little to no bugs, and a plethora of characters to choose from. The custom game mode is enjoyable with friends, matchmaking is quick for queues and gametime, and the game is welcoming to new players. Not to mention, the game is literally free, with no "pay-to-win" features other than some really cool skins that will make you feel inferior.

Issue/Gripe: The only real issue I've had with this game is the price of skins (as with most games) and the fact that you can't queue for duos by yourself. Instead, you MUST have someone added and in your lobby to play anything other than solos in ranked.

review: I’ve spent a ton of time in Brawlhalla, and honestly, it just keeps getting better. The gameplay is so smooth and the mechanics are easy enough to learn, but there’s a lot of depth once you get into the nuances. It’s one of those games where you can pick it up casually, but then, once you start mastering characters and combos, it gets pretty addictive. The roster of legends is huge, and each one feels distinct, so there’s always someone new to try out. Plus, the updates are great — they keep things fresh, whether it’s with new characters, skins, or game modes. If you like fast-paced, strategic brawling with a lot of variety, this is definitely worth your time. I’ve put hours into it, and I’m still having a blast!

The problem for me is the overpowered brawlers that come out every time and end up being heavily nerfed. Another issue is the bugs where me or my friends will hit someone else and the hit registers with the color but does no damage. This can happen multiple times a match, leading to a loss or just barely grasping victory. I've experienced this since December 2024. Other than that, I've enjoyed the game a lot and played with my friends in private matches due to the atrocious community and sweaty ranked modes. I'd absolutely recommend the game.

review:
Brawlhalla: The Game Where You Punch, Kick, and Throw Your Friends Into Oblivion (and Maybe Your Own Self-Esteem)

So, you’ve decided to enter the world of Brawlhalla? Prepare yourself for a brawler experience that is as chaotic as a family reunion on Thanksgiving, but with more flying fists and less passive-aggressive comments about your life choices. This is the game where you get to pummel your friends into submission (or just get pummelled, if you’re like me), all in the name of victory and bragging rights. Oh, and there are also weapons. Lots of them.

In Brawlhalla, you choose from a diverse cast of characters, each one with their own special abilities that seem as if they were designed by a committee that didn’t get enough sleep. You’ve got knights with oversized swords, random space aliens with energy blasters, and even characters that look like they walked straight out of a fantasy novel. And no matter who you pick, you’ll still probably end up getting knocked out by someone using the character that looks like they’ve never even seen a weapon before. Don’t worry, it’s a learning experience.

The combat? Pure chaos. There’s no subtlety here. You’re not learning the ancient art of martial arts—you’re just wildly flailing, hoping that your opponent doesn’t dodge, counter, or do literally anything that requires skill. Your best friend is the spam button. What’s that? A random combo of attacks that somehow works? Perfect. You’ve unlocked the next level of Brawlhalla mastery, which means you now look like you know what you’re doing... until you get knocked off the stage and sent into the void. RIP.

Now, let’s talk about the stages. They’re not your typical “let’s fight on a solid ground” kind of place. Oh no. Instead, you’re fighting on floating platforms, in arenas with giant moving obstacles, or in places where the very ground beneath your feet is constantly trying to kill you. Every stage is an obstacle course, and you’ll spend 90% of the match either jumping over gaps or falling into one. That moment when you think you’re winning only to get blasted off the edge? Yeah, that’s a classic. You’ll feel like you’ve won, but then you see your opponent casually float back on and it’s just... devastating.

Items? Oh, don’t get me started. They’re not “power-ups” like in other games. They’re random chaos generators that fall from the sky like an insane game of loot roulette. Want a sword? Boom! It’s there. Want a rocket launcher that sends your friend flying off the edge? Sure, why not? And if you’re lucky (or unlucky), you’ll end up getting some ridiculous weapon like a giant hammer that somehow makes you both look ridiculous and overpowered. But let’s be honest, we all know the true MVP weapon here is the “bomb,” which you will inevitably throw at your own face in a moment of sheer panic. Classic.

The multiplayer aspect? It’s a free-for-all. Brawlhalla’s multiplayer feels like a drunken brawl in the middle of a dance floor—everyone’s swinging, everyone’s confused, and in the end, no one knows how they won. But that’s the beauty of it. Brawlhalla is a game that’s all about embracing the chaos and pretending like you know what you’re doing. Even if you don’t, there’s always that sweet, sweet feeling when you knock someone else out... only to immediately get destroyed by someone else. The endless cycle of victory and embarrassment is what keeps us all coming back for more.

And if you want to take it up a notch, Brawlhalla lets you test your skills in a ranked mode where you can earn those sweet bragging rights by winning matches... or just continually falling off the map like an absolute pro. It’s a great feeling to see your rank go up, especially when you manage to pull off some crazy combo (and by crazy, I mean “I have no idea how I did that”). If you’re lucky, you’ll even end up playing against a true expert who will humiliate you for the next hour, but hey, it’s all about the experience, right?

In conclusion, Brawlhalla is a chaotic, fast-paced, and surprisingly fun game where the only real strategy is to survive longer than your friends and hope your wild button mashing somehow results in victory. Whether you’re playing solo, with friends, or against strangers who seem way too good at this game, Brawlhalla is the perfect way to throw your hands in the air, scream at your screen, and forget all your real-life responsibilities—because it’s just that fun.
